tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Use this when a search result looks relevant and you need its full text before answering. Takes the id returned by search, and returns the memory with its url, which you cite in your answer. Do not call it with an id from anywhere else: only search results carry valid ids.

tools.name: cortex_recall
tools.description: Use this when the user asks about a topic as a whole ("what do you know about X", "where are we with X", "catch me up on X"): returns one narrative synthesis of the relevant memories, saying what holds now and what was superseded. Do not use it to look up a single fact or when you need sources to ci

tools.name: cortex_write
tools.description: Use this when the user explicitly asks you to remember, note down, keep or save something, in any language: save the requested content within all the limits below. If they ask to save an idea or draft, preserve its provisional status. Within the user's authorized use of Cortex for ongoing memory, al

tools.name: cortex_write_status
tools.description: Use this when a previous cortex_write returned a job_id as queued and the user asks whether it was saved: returns the quality gate verdict for that job and any contradiction it opened. Do not call it for a write that already came back with a verdict.

tools.name: cortex_forget
tools.description: Use this when the user asks to delete a specific memory, given the id returned by search. Ask the user to confirm before calling it: the deletion is permanent and cannot be undone. Do not use it to fix a memory that is merely out of date: saving the corrected version with cortex_write is what keeps

tools.name: cortex_conflicts
tools.description: Use this when the user asks what contradicts what in their memory, or when a memory you just read is flagged as conflicting and the user has to decide which version holds. findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "fetch" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search, fetch, cortex_recall · Private data: search, cortex_write · Public sink: cortex_write · Destructive: search, cortex_forget.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search, fetch, cortex_recall · Private data: search, cortex_write · Public sink: cortex_write · Destructive: search, cortex_forget

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
